subject: Onboarding: PII mapping, export gating & access trace requirements
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@stratushealth.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Colin Park <colin.park@stratushealth.com>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: PII mapping and export gating for onboarding

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the quick demo yesterday. We are starting legal/security intake for the integration and need a few artifacts to close our internal onboarding checklist:

- A PII field mapping that shows which model inputs are treated as identifiers vs. metadata (CSV/PDF is fine).
- A dataflow diagram with export boundaries called out (what leaves our region and where).
- KMS custody and key rotation notes (who holds keys for customer-data-at-rest and any HSM/KMS partners).
- Any redaction or minimization options available at ingest and at inference time.

Can you share these by EOD Friday? We have a compliance gate next Tuesday and need to attach evidence. If there are known gaps, please call them out and propose mitigations.

Also, we'll likely ask for an attestation for cross-border exports and a recent SOC2 summary once the mapping is submitted.

Thanks — Elena
Elena Morales
Sr. Security PM, Stratus Health
elena.morales@stratushealth.com

Attachments: none (initial request)

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@stratushealth.com>
Cc: Colin Park <colin.park@stratushealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 13:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PII mapping and export gating for onboarding

Elena — thanks for the clear list. We're on it. Quick plan and deliverables:

1) PII mapping: we'll provide a CSV mapping fields -> sensitivity classification -> retention tier by Friday (pii_mapping_v1.pdf attached).
2) Dataflow diagram: attached PNG with region boundaries highlighted (dataflow_diagram_v2.png).
3) KMS note: short write-up in the Drive folder with key custody model; high-level: Redwood holds application encryption keys in customer-dedicated KMS when configured for Private deployments; for hosted customers we use customer-managed keys via the KMS integration where requested. We'll include rotation cadence and proof points.
4) Minimization/redaction: see attached redaction_plan.docx; we describe prefix-based redaction and token-level suppression options plus recommended canary prompts for sensitive fields.

I've uploaded everything to a shared Drive folder and included a readme with suggested evidence to attach to your intake. Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-llm-onboarding

If you want, Marissa (privacy) and Ben (infra) can jump on a short call Friday morning to walk the artifacts. Otherwise we'll send the final zipped evidence by COB Friday.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.com

Attachments: pii_mapping_v1.pdf (PDF), dataflow_diagram_v2.png (image), redaction_plan.docx (docx)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Morales <elena.morales@stratushealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 08:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PII mapping and export gating for onboarding

Grace / Elena — adding a few clarifying points from the privacy team before we finalize:

- The mapping in pii_mapping_v1.pdf currently marks device identifiers and full names as high sensitivity; we recommend an optional pseudonymization step at ingest for any field marked HIGH to reduce export risk. See 'redaction_plan.docx' section 2.
- Export gating: the diagram shows two possible egress paths (hosted multi-tenant vs. private VPC). For Stratus Health I recommend:
  * Default: route to Dedicated in us-west (no cross-border export).
  * If Private requested: customer-managed KMS + isolated VPC (documented with network CIDR and egress specs).
- Evidence: attaching a short SOC2 summary (soc2_summary_2026.pdf) and a KMS attestation template we'll sign for Private customers.

I've created JIRA ticket JIRA-PRIV-879 to track the evidence handover and to capture any redlines your legal team requests. I'll drop a brief note into the Drive readme with the specific artifact names we'll need to prove (e.g., rotation logs, audit log excerpts).

If Stratus wants an in-person walkthrough, we're available Friday 10:00–11:00 PT.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Privacy Ops
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachments: soc2_summary_2026.pdf (PDF)

From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@stratushealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Colin Park <colin.park@stratushealth.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 11:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PII mapping and export gating for onboarding

Thanks — this is perfect and in-scope for our gate. We'll review the Drive artifacts now. Two quick asks before the call Friday:

1) Please include an excerpt of rotation logs (anonymized) or a rotation policy snapshot showing the last rotation date. It's fine to redact key material; we just need proof of cadence.
2) Send the KMS attestation template you mentioned (we need something to attach to our legal intake).

If you can push those into the Drive and update JIRA-PRIV-879, we'll approve the intake contingent on the SOC2 summary and the rotation evidence.

On the call: we'll likely ask about the fallback routing (what happens if Dedicated capacity is exhausted) and whether an automatic model downgrade for throughput would cause any retention/transfer changes.

Best,
Elena
